title: The Escarpment of Devil's Throat
premise: Zephyrine Hartwell, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted in Peru and Bolivia, is hired off the books by a mining company to trace an expedition that went silent near the Devil's Throat escarpment, a forbidden gorge sacred to the Ashaninka and rumored to hold her late father's lost survey cache. Following the river upstream with a defrocked archaeologist and the expedition's lone survivor, she discovers the missing team was murdered to conceal a pre-Columbian city and a forged land claim implicating her father. Betrayed by her employer and hunted through the gorge, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth at the cost of the valley's secrecy or letting her father's name stay buried; she burns the claim, saves the survivor, and finally stops running.
about_author: Kestrel Hartwell is the pen name of a former river outfitter who spent a decade guiding on Andean headwaters before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who can't go home.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Blacklisted and broke in a border town, she takes cash from a mining fixer to find a silent expedition upriver. She almost refuses—her father died on that river—but debt decides for her. Beat: restless resignation.

chapters.title: Dead Radio
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She reaches the last known camp: tents slashed, radio smashed, one grave dug too shallow. Tracks lead toward the Devil's Throat escarpment, where no guide will follow. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She finds Tomás Quispe, the expedition's junior surveyor, feverish and hiding in a hollow tree, clutching a brass theodolite stamped with her father's initials. He begs her not to take him back downriver. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What Tomás Saw
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV, fragmented by fever. He recounts the expedition leader, Voss, finding a stone causeway above the gorge—and then men with company rifles turning on the crew. Beat: horror reframing the mission as flight, not rescue.

chapters.title: Hired to Bury It
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She realizes she wasn't hired to rescue anyone but to confirm the deaths and recover Voss's documents. The fixer's satellite phone rings; she lets it ring out. Beat: betrayal understood, trust in nothing.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She and Tomás abandon the trail and push upriver by raft through rapids, pursued by the company's security chief, Rennick, and his men. Beat: kinetic momentum, first taste of partnership.

chapters.title: The Ashaninka Guide
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Captured by Ashaninka river guards, she bargains in broken Quechua; an elder woman, Naira, recognizes her father's name—the man who mapped their territory honestly when others lied. Beat: inheritance as burden and gift.

chapters.title: Naira's Price
chapters.summary: Naira's POV. The elder agrees to guide them to the escarpment if Zephyrine swears the valley stays unclaimed, whatever her father's papers say. Zephyrine hesitates—her whole life is built on his legend. Beat: duty versus love made literal.

chapters.title: Rennick's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. The security chief reviews the file: Hartwell senior found the city, refused to sign the claim, and died conveniently. Zephyrine is leverage and loose end both. Beat: cold menace, stakes clarified.

chapters.title: The Causeway
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Above the gorge they find the hidden stair her father carved, his marks still fresh after twenty years. Tomás deciphers the survey notes: the city is real, and the claim is forged over Ashaninka land. Beat: awe and grief entwined.

chapters.title: The Escarpment of Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They cross beneath the roaring falls into terraces of ruins—roads, reservoirs, a civilization the river kept secret. For one night it feels like coming home. Beat: wonder, the calm before.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Rennick's men catch them at the narrows; Naira is wounded covering the escape, and Tomás is taken with the survey notes. Zephyrine escapes alone into the gorge. Beat: devastating loss, guilt igniting purpose.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Rennick offers Tomás his life for a signed statement pinning everything on Hartwell's daughter. Tomás stalls, buying hours, learning Rennick fears the fixer more than the jungle. Beat: fear transmuted into cunning.

chapters.title: The Fixer Arrives
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The mining fixer lands by helicopter—not to help Rennick but to erase him too; the claim was never sanctioned. Zephyrine eavesdrops from the cliffs and understands everyone above her is expendable. Beat: vertigo of scale.

chapters.title: Alone in the Gorge
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Wounded, half-starved, she follows her father's old route markers through the gorge by memory she never knew she had—his journal passages surfacing word for word. Beat: memory as inheritance, grief becoming strength.

chapters.title: Rescue Reversed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She frees Tomás from the camp at night, and he chooses to come back for her rather than run—a mirror of chapter three. Naira's people shadow them, armed now. Beat: love against duty, chosen twice.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In a sealed chamber they find her father's true survey: honest maps, and a letter naming the forgery he refused to sign, addressed to 'my daughter, if she ever stops moving.' Beat: emotional climax of inheritance.

chapters.title: Rennick's Last Ascent
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Cornered by his own employers, Rennick goes rogue, seizing the cache and Naira as hostages to bargain his way out with the claim intact. Beat: desperation, ticking clock.

chapters.title: Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the escarpment lip in a storm, she trades herself for Naira, then uses the gorge's rope routes—her father's routes—to turn the trap, sending Rennick's evidence and nearly Rennick into the falls. Beat: climax, skill and sacrifice fused.

chapters.title: What Survives the River
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The fixer's operation collapses under its own erasures; officials arrive to find only the honest maps, which Zephyrine surrenders to Naira's people, keeping the city's location unwritten. Beat: costly victory, love proven by what she gives up.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. In Lima, Tomás testifies; the blacklist on Hartwell's name dissolves into something quieter—an apology no one quite says. Zephyrine watches from the gallery, anonymous by choice. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Stopping Costs Nothing Now
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She returns to the river as a guide for Naira's community, teaching their young people the water she once fled. At her father's marked tree she plants the theodolite like a seed. Beat: resolution—stillness chosen, memory carried forward.
